items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was engaged by Willy de Cort, president of the Belgium Hot Club to play a concert at the Galeries des Beaux Arts in Brussels.

ctx.x: We also had a visit of Tommy Dorsey one night. I had seen Tommy and heard some of his orchestras in the Apple, but had never met him. Someone asked him to sit in with us and although he did not have his trombone with him, he tried the one that Charles Huss had and found out that it was a good instrument, so he played a couple of numbers with us. I told him that I played in Sy Oliver's orchestra before I came to France and he was quite well pleased to hear that, as Sy had been his arranger for a few years. There…

At times I would have a gig out of town for which I would inform the artistic director of the club, whose name was Guy Masse. In March, 1952, on a certain date, I was engaged by Willy de Cort, president of the Belgium Hot Club to play a concert at the Galeries des Beaux Arts in Brussels. Don Byas and Art Simmen were also engaged for this deal. I don't remember the rest of the musicians. Another organisation had organised a concert with Sidney Bechet and as Willy was the first and biggest organiser or jazz…

A few nights before I was to play in Brussels, some young fellows came to the club St. Germain and asked me if I could be engaged to play a few numbers on a river barge which they had transformed into a club. I told them they would have to get permission from Guy Masse and he gave it. The concert in Brussels was on a Sunday night and this thing on the barge was the following Monday night. I returned to Paris that Monday afternoon and played one set at the club St. Germain. Someone from the barge came to get me…
